subject: Transformed Parameter Block Subset of a Matrix

messages.author: 6d020fc5d7c9ee0a
messages.subject: Transformed Parameter Block Subset of a Matrix
parts:
Hi,

I have created a matrix of my regression coefficients using vector[3] beta[J], where I have J groups of parameters.  Two of the coefficient are on harmonic terms, and I would like Rstan to return the amplitude using r= sqrt(b2^2+b3^2) for each group.  I am just uncertain how to select the 2nd and 3rd parameter from the matrix as it is constructed.  E.g., if I want to get the 2nd parameter for the ith group, I have tried beta[2,i]; however, this indexing doesn't seem to work, as it might in R.  Any suggestions would be much appreciated.

Thanks,

Colin

parameters { 
vector[3] gamma; // 3 Beta Coefficients 
  vector<lower=0> [3] tau; //SD of the regression coefficients
  vector[3] beta[J]; //matrix of group-level regression coefficients
  real<lower=0> sigma; //standard deviation of the y's
}

transformed parameters{
  real amp[J];
  for (i in 1:J){
  amp[i] = sqrt(beta[2,i]^2 + beta[3,i]^2);
  print(amp[i]);
  }
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Transformed Parameter Block Subset of a Matrix
parts:
> On Apr 14, 2017, at 12:49 PM, Colin <clewi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I have created a matrix of my regression coefficients using vector[3] beta[J], where I have J groups of parameters. Two of the coefficient are on harmonic terms, and I would like Rstan to return the amplitude using r= sqrt(b2^2+b3^2) for each group. I am just uncertain how to select the 2nd and 3rd parameter from the matrix as it is constructed. E.g., if I want to get the 2nd parameter for the ith group, I have tried beta[2,i]; however, this indexing doesn't seem to work, as it might in R.

Matrix indexing works just like in R, so I'm not sure what the
problem is.

> Any suggestions would be much appreciated.
>
> Thanks,
>
> Colin
>
> parameters {
> vector[3] gamma; // 3 Beta Coefficients
> vector<lower=0> [3] tau; //SD of the regression coefficients
> vector[3] beta[J]; //matrix of group-level regression coefficients

This is an array of vectors, not a matrix. But the indexing you have
will still work. The model won't work because there's no distributions
put on these unconstrained parameters.

> real<lower=0> sigma; //standard deviation of the y's
> }
>
> transformed parameters{
> real amp[J];
> for (i in 1:J){
> amp[i] = sqrt(beta[2,i]^2 + beta[3,i]^2);

We have a hypoteneuse function, so you could just write

amp[i] = hypot(beta[2, i], beta[3, i]);

- Bob

Thanks, Bob.  This was helpful.  I flipped the indexing around and that seems to have worked.   I will also add that hypot function.    Yes, I am sorry I didn't include the full code before, but I do have priors on all the parameters, and the model seems to be working well now.

~Colin

data {
  int<lower=1> N; //the number of observations
  int<lower=1> J; //the number of pixels
  int<lower=1> K; //Number of Covariates
  int<lower=1,upper=J> id[N]; // vector of group index
  matrix[N,K] x; //the model matrix
  vector[N] y; // 
}


parameters {
  vector[K] gamma; // K Beta Coefficients 
  vector<lower=0> [K] tau; //SD of the regression coefficients

  vector[K] beta[J]; //matrix of group-level regression coefficients

real<lower=0> sigma; //standard deviation of the y's
}

transformed parameters{
  real amp[J];
  for (i in 1:J){

amp[i] = sqrt(beta[i,2]^2 + beta[i,3]^2);
  }
}

model {
  vector[N] mu; //linear predictor
  
  //priors
  gamma ~ normal(0,5); //Priors on Beta's, Assuming Independence 
  tau ~ cauchy(0,1); 
  sigma ~ cauchy(0,1); 
  
  for(j in 1:J){
   beta[j] ~ normal(gamma,tau); 
  }
  
  for(n in 1:N){
        mu[n] = x[n] * beta[id[n]]; 
        }
  //likelihood
  y ~ normal(mu,sigma);

}
